newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore diesel firmer on Indian import volumes.
newsitem.headline: Singapore diesel firmer on Indian import volumes.

text.p: Singapore diesel prices rose on increased buying from India but the hike was tempered by aggressive selling by a Singapore trader, industry sources said on Monday.
Traders said November swaps rose to trade at an intra-day high of $30.70 before easing to $30.45 as a result of offers from the Singapore trader. November swaps closed at $30.25/30.35 on Friday.
The Singapore trader sold two 150,000-barrel cargoes at $30.50 and $30.40 fob Singapore to a Thai trader and a Meditterrenean trader.

The market firmed earlier Monday following confirmation of India's large purchase of 520,000-tonnes for arrival in December. Rumours were rife on Friday that India would buy up to 600,000-tonnes and the swaps market firmed as a result. Traders said the market is also receiving support from Indonesia and China who were still seeking November cargoes.

Part of Saudi Aramco's 1997 term tender for 0.5 percent gas oil was settled at premium of around $1 to MidEast spot quotes, traders said. Jet fuel remained depressed on ample supplies in Singapore with major offering at parity to Singapore quotes and trader offered at $30.85 against a bid at $30.20 per barrel.

Naphtha firmed with crude and swaps amid thin talk. Traders said they expected more activity this week when players return from term talks with Aramco. November swaps firmed to $22.40/$22.60 from Friday's $22.05/$22.10.

Gasoline edged up with crude in a one-sided market. Only buyers emerged with bids for a 92-octane unleaded cargo at $24.40 a barrel fob Singapore, and a 97-octane unleaded at $26.10. Chinese refiners were heard to have emerged to offer December low-octane barrels but no levels were heard. Fuel oil firmed on buying from a trader. A 20,000-tonne cargo traded at $118 per tonne fob Singapore. --Singapore Newsroom (+65-8703093)
